feature: HTTP/2 WebTransport server owner admission and failure rollback

behavior.budget: EndpointServer.initWithDeadline transfers ownership on entry and applies one caller deadline/cancellation through fixed-table allocation and owner admission, with checks before tables, before worker assignment and after startup
behavior.rollback: failed or late candidates close abortively without protocol shutdown output; already assigned workers are stopped and joined before owner allocation is released
behavior.accept: cleartext/TLS deadline accept constructors pass the same original deadline to owner initialization
behavior.listener: managed-owner initialization after raw acceptance receives the configured endpoint operation timeout; Canceled releases its connection reservation and terminates the accept worker
behavior.structure: client/server worker assignment and rollback share endpoint/initialization.zig; server table construction is isolated in endpoint_server/init.zig

python_interop_debug.scope: normal queue/admission, pending cleanup, generation reuse and full Capsule exchange after successful deadline adoption; failure cases are exercised by the module socket-backed regressions

verification.case_invariants: original error is preserved, no worker is assigned when budget/cancellation fails before startup, late/canceled started candidates are joined, provisional raw TCP reaches EOF without protocol bytes, and leak-checking allocator releases all tables
verification.allocation_sweep: checkAllAllocationFailures over deadline adoption and abortive owner destruction
verification.listener_cancellation: raw HTTP/2 acceptance completes, the first managed allocation arms owner-admission cancellation, accept group must join within the test budget and release its one connection reservation with no installed connection
verification.existing_coverage: client reconnect completion, TLS server/listener multi-connection flow, pending request cleanup and independent client/server queues remain in the complete HTTP2 WebTransport gate

limitations: final owner destruction still joins cooperative I/O tasks; this evidence does not claim preemption of arbitrary custom allocator or I/O callbacks
listener reservation, connection-table publication/lookup and close pacing retain separate lifecycle budgets
broader protocol integration and multi-hour/high-concurrency evidence remain open for the overall library goal
